Increase Contrast listing copy vs contrast engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate system accessibility features with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Increase Contrast on the device — iOS applies stronger borders, fills, and separators on buttons, icons, and system UI chrome so controls read more clearly without enlarging text. Toggle under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Increase Contrast. System accessibility behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • UIAccessibility contrast and in-app contrast APIs — code that detects or responds to Increase Contrast, adapts custom controls, or ships companion contrast demos. Engineering inside the binary — not listing rewrite.
  • Increase Contrast marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app works with Increase Contrast, respects higher UI contrast, or improves readability when system contrast is on. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Increase Contrast.

An app that references Increase Contrast in onboarding and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe higher UI contrast and readability on the store page, not whether Increase Contrast toggles inside iOS Settings.

Increase Contrast-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

UI-contrast marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Increase Contrast in iOS Settings — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 增强对比度 for Increase Contrast, with related buyer language around 提高对比度 (increase contrast), 对比度 (contrast), 显示与文字大小 (Display & Text Size under 辅助功能 → 无障碍), and 可读性 (readability). Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic 视力 or medical eye-exam claims that could imply clinical products.

Increase Contrast vs Display Accommodations color filters

Color filters, smart invert, and reduce white point live under Accessibility → Display & Text Size alongside Increase Contrast — but they are different features with different buyer intent. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 颜色滤镜 or 降低白点 when your English source only shows an Increase Contrast toggle. See the Display Accommodations listing guide only if color filters are your lead marketing claim.

Increase Contrast vs Accessibility Zoom and Magnifier

Accessibility Zoom enlarges on-screen UI — 缩放. Magnifier magnifies physical objects through the camera — 放大镜. Increase Contrast strengthens button, icon, and separator contrast — 增强对比度. If your English gallery shows a zoom slider, do not upgrade zh-Hans copy to 增强对比度 claims. See the Accessibility Zoom listing guide or Magnifier listing guide only if magnification is your lead marketing claim.

Increase Contrast vs Screen Distance and Reduce Motion

Screen Distance detects physical viewing distance — 屏幕距离. Reduce Motion tones down animations — 减少动态效果. Increase Contrast adjusts UI element contrast — 增强对比度. If your English gallery shows a too-close alert or motion-reduction badge, do not upgrade zh-Hans copy to 对比度 claims unless that is what the frame shows. See the Screen Distance listing guide or Reduce Motion listing guide only if those are your lead marketing claims.

Increase Contrast vs True Tone, Night Shift, and Dark Mode

True Tone adjusts white balance — 原彩显示. Night Shift shifts evening warmth — 夜览. Dark Mode changes UI appearance — 深色模式. Increase Contrast sharpens control borders — 增强对比度. If your English gallery shows a color-temperature slider or dark-theme mockup, do not upgrade zh-Hans copy to 提高对比度 claims unless contrast is what the frame depicts. See the True Tone listing guide, Night Shift listing guide, or Dark Mode listing guide only if display color or appearance features are your lead marketing claim.

AppLocale FAQ

Is Increase Contrast the same as Display Accommodations color filters?

No. Increase Contrast boosts UI element contrast for buttons, icons, and separators — 增强对比度, 提高对比度. Display Accommodations covers color filters, invert colors, and reduce white point — 颜色滤镜, 降低白点. See our Display Accommodations listing guide for color-filter marketing copy.

Is Increase Contrast the same as Accessibility Zoom or Magnifier?

No. Accessibility Zoom and Magnifier market screen or camera magnification — 缩放, 放大镜. Increase Contrast markets higher UI contrast for readability — 增强对比度. See our Accessibility Zoom listing guide or Magnifier listing guide for magnification copy.

Is Increase Contrast the same as Screen Distance or Reduce Motion?

No. Screen Distance markets too-close viewing-distance reminders — 屏幕距离. Reduce Motion markets toned-down animations — 减少动态效果. Increase Contrast markets UI contrast boosts — 增强对比度. See our Screen Distance listing guide or Reduce Motion listing guide for those claims.

Is Increase Contrast the same as True Tone, Night Shift, or Dark Mode?

No. True Tone, Night Shift, and Dark Mode market display color and appearance — 原彩显示, 夜览, 深色模式. Increase Contrast markets UI element contrast — 增强对比度. See our True Tone listing guide, Night Shift listing guide, or Dark Mode listing guide for display color and appearance copy.
